label: baseline-haiku
reply:
**Status:** Referred to a claims handler. The police report has also been requested from the customer.

**Claim reference:** baseline-haiku-CLM-C

**Facts recorded**
- Policyholder: Ines Haddad, policy VER-1003, Toyota Yaris (2019), market value €9,000, licence held since 2015-03-20.
- Coverage claimed: C4 Theft. It is listed in the Policy Schedule.
- Incident: theft from the street in front of her building on 2026-10-15, while she was travelling.
- Report date: 2026-10-19 (email date), 4 days after the incident.
- No police report yet. No documents attached. No third party involved.

**Reasoning**
- **Coverage:** C4 Theft is in the Policy Schedule, so the claim falls under a covered coverage. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="Veridia contract"/> (Article 2 requires the coverage to be listed in the Policy Schedule.)
- **Late report:** Theft must be reported within 2 days of its discovery. The email is dated 4 days after the theft, and the discovery date is not stated. If the theft was discovered on 15 October, the claim is late. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="Veridia contract"/> (Article 4.1.) A late claim is never refused automatically; it goes to a claims handler. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="3" name="Veridia contract"/> (Article 7.1.)
- **Missing document:** Theft (C4) requires a police report. The customer has not filed one. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="Veridia contract"/> (Article 4.3.) A missing document is requested from the policyholder, not used to refuse the claim. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="Veridia contract"/> (Article 4.3.) The police report was requested through the claims system.
- **Possible exclusion:** None indicated by the email. The story does not show alcohol, licence, racing, intentional damage or wear. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="Veridia contract"/> (Article 3.) Exclusions are never applied automatically in any case. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="Veridia contract"/> (Article 3.)
- **Money:** Not computed. The claim has a blocking issue (late report), so no settlement was calculated or staged. Nothing has been approved or paid.

**Amounts**
- Not computed. For reference only, the contract sets theft at 10% of the claim, minimum €500, with the claim amount equal to market value. <cite document_id="2630#10255" pages="2" name="Veridia contract"/> A handler will confirm the figures once the claim is reviewed.

**Actions in the claims system**
- `get_policy` (VER-1003): policy details returned as above.
- `create_claim` (C4, incident 2026-10-15, reported 2026-10-19): claim opened. Blocking issues: `late_report` and `missing_document:police_report`.
- `escalate_to_handler` (late_report, other): referred to a Veridia claims handler. Do not settle.
- `request_documents` (police_report): requested from the customer. Claim status is escalated.
- Not performed: `compute_settlement`, `stage_settlement`, `schedule_assessor`.

**Note:** The subagent's first pass cited contract articles it could not verify. I checked the contract directly and the references above are confirmed.

**Draft message to the customer**

> Dear Ms Haddad,
>
> Thank you for reporting the theft of your Toyota Yaris on 15 October 2026 under policy VER-1003. Your claim has been passed to a Veridia claims handler, who will review the report date. Please file a police report for the theft and send us a copy as soon as you can. We will contact you once the review is complete.
>
> Kind regards,
> Veridia Claims
